findings.title: Role grants the resource but not its subresource
findings.cause: container shipper exits because the API server refuses its ServiceAccount log-shipper: it may not get pods/log in namespace kd-rbac-subresource-log. Role pod-reader grants get, list on pods, and the request is for its log subresource, pods/log, which a rule grants only by that name (or "pods/*"): a rule that names pods covers the objects, not their subresources; its log says: "pods \"web-b665dbb8b-bwsrh\" is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-subresource-log:log-shipper\" cannot get resource \"pods/log\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kd-rbac-subresource-log\""; Deployment log-shipper has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: Role pod-reader, bound by RoleBinding log-shipper-pod-reader: apiGroups [""], resources ["pods"], verbs ["get", "list"]
evidence.command: kubectl get role pod-reader -n kd-rbac-subresource-log -o jsonpath='{.rules}'

evidence.what: RoleBinding log-shipper-pod-reader grants Role pod-reader to ServiceAccount log-shipper

findings.fix: Add "pods/log" to the resources of the rule of Role pod-reader that names pods (with verb get).
